source.title: Characterization of innexin gene expression and functional roles of gap-junctional communication in planarian regeneration
source.location: Table 1 (raw counts) and bar graph; Fig 10I images

injury: four transverse cuts giving head, pre-pharyngeal, trunk, post-pharyngeal and tail fragments

intervention.timing: immediately before amputation, through first 2 days
intervention.description: heptanol 0.0045-0.006% (v/v) in spring water from just before transverse amputation for 2 days, then washed into worm water

readout.method: stereomicroscope scoring of the posterior blastema regenerate of each fragment

notes: Table 1 raw counts: weak anteriorization (missing tail or bipolar pharynx) 9 + stronger anteriorization (incomplete ectopic head with eye structures) 0 coded as other; complete anteriorization (bipolar head with 2 eyes) 0 coded double_head. Scored at 14-20 days on posterior blastema of the original fragment. Dose range given as 0.0045-0.006% in methods (text also says 1-10 uM). ADJ: Table 1 counts confirmed against the table. Weak anteriorization (missing tail or bipolar pharynx) is a mixed partial class and is kept in other with stronger anteriorization (incomplete ectopic head). Dose given only as a range (0.0045-0.006%), so flagged pooled.

source.title: Characterization of innexin gene expression and functional roles of gap-junctional communication in planarian regeneration
source.location: Table 1 trunk column (raw counts, n=111, 14-20 days) and Fig 10III legend / Results text (43%, n=423, 7 days)

injury: four transverse cuts giving head, pre-pharyngeal, trunk, post-pharyngeal and tail fragments

intervention.timing: immediately before amputation, through first 2 days
intervention.description: heptanol 0.0045-0.006% (v/v) in spring water from just before transverse amputation for 2 days, then washed into worm water

readout.method: stereomicroscope scoring of the posterior blastema regenerate of each fragment

notes: ADJ: the paper reports the heptanol trunk arm twice (Table 1 trunk column, n=111: normal 35, weak 65, stronger 6, complete 5; and Fig 10III/Results, n=423: 43% anteriorized). Same agent, exposure and fragment type, so by the row rule these are repeats of ONE arm and are summed. n=423 report converted from percentages: 57% normal = 241; complete bipolar heads 16% (Results text; Fig 10III two-head bar segment also reads about 16%) = 68 coded double_head; legend strong class 18% minus 16% complete = 2% (8) incomplete two-head forms, plus weak class 25% (106: two pharynxes but no head or cyclops head at posterior end) coded other. Totals: normal 35+241; double_head 5+68; other = weak anteriorization 65+106 (missing tail / bipolar pharynx / no or cyclops head at posterior) + incomplete ectopic head 6+8. Scoring day differs between the two reports. Dose given only as a range, flagged pooled.

source.title: Characterization of innexin gene expression and functional roles of gap-junctional communication in planarian regeneration
source.location: Fig 10III bar graph and legend (20% incidence)

injury: transverse cuts anterior and posterior to the pharynx

intervention.timing: immediately before amputation, through first 2 days
intervention.description: hexanol 0.0045-0.006% (v/v) in spring water from just before transverse amputation for 2 days, then washed into worm water

readout.method: stereomicroscope scoring of the posterior blastema regenerate of each fragment

notes: Legend: hexanol 20% incidence of the weakest anteriorization class (inhibited tail regeneration), coded other as for the heptanol weak class. Scoring scheme (normal / weak / stronger / complete) is exhaustive and the text excludes the stronger classes, so the remaining 80% is normal (Fig 10III bar agrees, normal segment ends at the 80% gridline). n not stated.
remainder_quote: Exposure to hexanol, a reagent similar to heptanol but which is much less effective at blocking GJC than heptanol (Weingart and Bukauskas, 1998), never induced strong anteriorization of the posterior blastema but did inhibit tail regeneration (the weakest class of anteriorization)
